items.heading: Physiotherapy Has Real, Growing Scope
items.text: Physiotherapy has real, growing scope in India, an aging population, a rising sports and fitness culture, higher post-surgical rehab volume, and a fast-expanding home-healthcare segment are all pushing demand up. But the salary story most articles tell (a single "average salary" figure) hides the part that actually matters for your decision: which employer track you are on changes your income more than your degree does.

items.heading: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (Bpt)
items.text: The Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT) is the entry-level professional degree, regulated under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP). It runs 4.5 to 5 years total: four years of academic and clinical coursework, biomedical science foundations in year one, movement and therapy fundamentals in year two, system-specific physiotherapy in year three, and specialised applied physiotherapy in year four, followed by a compulsory one-year rotatory internship of at least 2,016 clinical hours.

items.heading: Ncahp Originally Proposed Making NEET
items.text: NCAHP originally proposed making NEET-UG the common entrance exam for BPT and BOT (Bachelor of Occupational Therapy) admissions starting the 2026-27 academic year.

items.heading: After Pushback From Institutions, Students,
items.text: After pushback from institutions, students, and professional bodies including the Indian Association of Physiotherapists, NCAHP deferred the NEET-mandatory requirement to the 2027-28 academic year.

items.heading: For the 2026
items.text: For the 2026-27 admission cycle, most institutions are admitting through a merit list based on aggregate Class 12 Physics, Chemistry, and Biology marks (commonly a minimum 50% aggregate), not NEET scores.
